title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This page is the canonical Redwood employee handbook section covering how we work at Redwood: role families and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding overview, and the primary internal tools new hires and current employees should know. It is intended for all employees and hiring managers and should be referenced during recruiting and onboarding processes.
introduction: Redwood Inference aims to be a high-velocity, developer-first company with a strong people-first culture. This document consolidates our expectations, career progression framework, benefits overview, and standard hiring and onboarding procedures. It is maintained by People Ops in partnership with Engineering and GTM leaders. Use links in Related Pages for team-specific policies and role-specific ladders.
roles_and_career_ladders:
Overview
- Role families: Engineering (serving-runtime, infra, platform, SRE, developer-experience), Product, Research & Applied ML, Design, Sales & GTM, Customer Success, People Ops, Finance & Legal.
- Career ladder structure: Individual Contributor (IC1 -> IC3 -> Senior -> Staff/Principal), Engineering Manager (EM1 -> EM2 -> Director), and Leadership paths.
- Promotion criteria (high level): impact, scope, technical or managerial leadership, cross-team influence, and execution reliability. Concrete signals include: consistent delivery of high-quality features, mentorship, design reviews ownership, incident leadership, and measurable product or cost improvements.
- Responsibilities by level (summary):
  - IC1–IC2: Deliver tasks with supervision, write clear PRs, participate in on-call rotations.
  - Senior IC: Own features or services end-to-end, mentor juniors, lead design docs, improve reliability or cost by measurable percent.
  - Staff/Principal: Drive cross-team initiatives, design architecture, lead performance or cost optimization programs, represent Redwood externally at conferences.
- Career conversations: Quarterly 1:1s should include career goals; managers run a formal calibration and growth plan review at least twice per year.
- Role-specific ladders and competencies: Link to team pages in Related Pages for engineering ladders, product PM levels, and applied ML research expectations.
benefits_and_perks:
Overview of core benefits (eligibility and enrollment windows included)
- Health & Wellness:
  - Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple tiers. Redwood covers 80% of employee-only premiums and 60% of dependent premiums (subject to change by regional plans).
  - Mental health: access to counseling sessions via our EAP, and 8 therapy sessions reimbursed per year for eligible employees.
  - Wellness stipend: $150 / quarter for home office or wellbeing expenses.
- Time off & Leave:
  - PTO: Flexible paid time off policy; recommended minimum accrual of 15 days/year for US employees with manager alignment.
  - Parental leave: Up to 20 weeks primary caregiver leave and 8 weeks secondary caregiver leave (local law permitting).
  - Public holidays: Core regional holidays plus floating holidays.
- Financial & Equity:
  - Competitive base salary with equity grants on hire and refresh cycles aligned to milestones.
  - 401(k) with company match for US employees. Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP) available.
- Career & Learning:
  - $2,000 annual learning stipend and dedicated discretionary training days.
  - Conference allowance and paid volunteer days for open-source contributions.
- Perks & Office:
  - Home office stipend on hire, commuter benefits in select locations, and catered weekly team lunches at HQ.
- How to enroll and questions: Contact People Ops at people-ops@redwood.com or use the Benefits tab in the HR portal. Enrollment windows are within 30 days of hire or during annual open enrollment.
- Exceptions and regional variations: See Related Pages for country-specific plan summaries.
hiring_and_onboarding_overview:
Hiring principles and standard process
- Principles: Hire for impact, clarity of role and success metrics, inclusive interviewing, and timely feedback. All roles must have a published job spec and hiring rubric before interviews begin.
- Hiring stages (standard):
  1) Requisition and job posting (owner: hiring manager + People Ops)
  2) Resume screen and recruiter phone screen (owner: recruiting)
  3) Technical / role exercise as appropriate (time-boxed; owner: hiring manager)
  4) Onsite / loop interviews (mix of hiring manager, peers, and cross-functional partners)
  5) Offer review and compensation calibration (People Ops + Finance)
  6) Offer delivery and acceptance
  7) Background checks and I-9 / local equivalents
- Interview rubrics: Each panel uses a standard rubric (skills, signals, culture add, role-specific competencies). Interviewers must submit feedback within 48 hours. Hiring managers coordinate calibration calls for borderline candidates.
- Diversity and inclusion: Sourcing and shortlisting should aim for diverse pipelines; panel composition guidance is provided in the Hiring Toolkit (Related Pages).
Onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
- Pre-start (People Ops + IT): account creation, equipment order, access requests (G Suite, Okta, Slack, JIRA, Confluence, internal dashboards), and welcome packet.
- Day 1: Welcome meeting with manager, HR orientation, security training, and team welcome lunch.
- Week 1: Core trainings (product overview, platform architecture primer, security & privacy basics), assigned onboarding buddy, and first 1:1 planned.
- Month 1: Deliver an onboarding project with clear acceptance criteria, attend cross-functional intro sessions, and start ownership of small scoped tasks.
- Month 2–3: Ramp goals set by manager (technical competence, on-call readiness if applicable, contribution to team roadmap), quarterly OKR alignment conversation, and onboarding retrospective.
- Onboarding resources: Standard playbooks and templates live under eng-developer-experience and eng-platform. Managers must complete the Manager Onboarding checklist for each new hire (linked in Related Pages).
Hiring & offer operational details
- Offer letters and salary bands: Use the central comp band table maintained by People Ops. Exceptions require VP approval.
- Notice periods and start date negotiation: Hiring managers coordinate with People Ops to respect candidate notice periods.
- Remote hiring and equipment shipping: For remote hires, hardware is shipped to the home address; IT verifies receipt on Day 1.
internal_tools_guides:
Primary internal tools and how we use them
- Identity & Access:
  - Okta: Single sign-on — primary entry for all SaaS apps. Request app access via the IAM form.
  - Google Workspace: Documents, calendar, and email. Share docs using groups where possible.
- Communication & Documentation:
  - Slack: Org-wide and team channels. Use #announcements for company-wide notices and threads for discussions.
  - Confluence: Canonical documentation location. All teams should maintain runbooks and decision records here. Page templates are available in the company-handbook space.
- Engineering & Product:
  - JIRA: Issue tracking and sprint planning. Use issue types: bug, story, task, and spike. Each sprint must have a defined sprint goal.
  - GitHub: Source-of-truth for repositories. Use protected branches, required PR reviews (min 2 for critical services), and CI checks.
  - Internal deployment dashboard: For Dedicated and Hosted services, the console lists active rollouts and model versions. Access requires role-based controls; see eng-platform runbooks for permissions.
- Observability & Incident Management:
  - Datadog: Metrics and dashboards. SLO dashboards live in the Redwood Observability folder.
  - PagerDuty: On-call routing and incident paging. Follow the oncall runbook for escalation steps.
- HR & Admin:
  - HR portal: Benefits enrollment, time off requests, and payroll info.
  - Ticketing system: Internal IT and facilities tickets go through the Helpdesk queue.
Tooling best practices and owner contacts
- Keep documentation current: When you change a service or workflow, update the Confluence page and add a summary to the change log.
- Owners: Each tool has a documented owner; for tool onboarding or permission issues, contact the listed owner on the tool's Confluence page. Common owners: IT (hardware & accounts), People Ops (HR portal), Eng Platform (deployment dashboard and CI), Security (IAM reviews).
- Access request process: Use the Access Request template in Confluence or the IAM form; approvals depend on the tool and role.
- Security note: Do not store secrets in Confluence or GitHub; use the company-approved secret manager.
faq:
Frequently asked questions
- Q: Who do I contact for benefits enrollment?
  A: People Ops at people-ops@redwood.com or use the HR portal.
- Q: How do promotion cycles work?
  A: Promotions are evaluated with calibration twice per year; talk to your manager about timing and evidence required.
- Q: What if I need special equipment?
  A: Submit an IT ticket and cc your manager. Exceptional hardware requests require manager approval and a business case.
- Q: Where are team-specific career ladders?
  A: See Related Pages; each engineering sub-team maintains a published ladder with competencies and examples.
